FFLOS gives 1922; Forest Lookouts gives only 192?? and a 1925 newspaper dates the fatal strike to 1924; the year is disputed
Fire guard Victor Ortega killed by lightning in the cabin on June 30, 1924

corrections.why: The FFLOS page gives an elevation of 10,913 ft (3,326 m) and no tower height. No source read gives 4.3 m.

resolved_conflicts.field: abandonment date and cause of death
resolved_conflicts.explanation: FFLOS says the tower was abandoned in 1922 after strikes, one killing the guard. Forest Lookouts gives the abandonment only as 192??; a January 1925 newspaper report it quotes, and the NRHP name-change record, date the fatal strike to June 30, 1924. The 1922 date is therefore disputed.

notes_for_editor: The brief's height_m 4.3 is not in any source read; the FFLOS page gives only the elevation, so removal is proposed. The brief's 1922 abandonment is the FFLOS date, but the fatal strike that the same FFLOS text links to it is dated June 30, 1924 by the 1925 newspaper and the NRHP record, so the year is flagged as disputed. The brief's claim that the cabin is the oldest surviving fire-detection structure in the region was not found in the sources read and is left out. No access or rental source was found, so access is omitted. The NRHP name-change sheet mentions an interpretive sign at the site without a date.
